body:
# the contributor audit: thin-edge obstruction to individual best-menu payment

Source: `candidate e52160c774656005`. Full read of Sections 1–9 and of its quantitative simplex and strip dependencies: PASS within the cited attained positive-width interface. An independent Rate audit also passes. This is an auxiliary counterexample, not a counterexample to OC.

The three fibers have a canonical full-dimensional convex realization. The Dirichlet slice calculation gives alpha=4 delta^3−3 delta^4 exactly. The middle source tends to the simplex centroid and is unique at positive width by the already proved full-normal identity. The ordinary simplex cap gap restricts ALL active continuous directions, not merely a chosen circuit, to the five vertex cones.

For the three low-coordinate cones, zero base tilt misses both endpoint fibers; actual minimization forces zero outside mass and coarea. For the two edge-coordinate cones, swapping those two barycentrics gives a volume-preserving pairing with uniformly positive summed margins. Thus outside mass is at least one endpoint volume for EVERY base tilt. A saturated tilt attains it. A transition strip of positive volume would give strictly greater mass, so every active cap has zero endpoint coarea. Continuity and connectedness also ensure its endpoint profile is either fully captured or fully missed. This justifies the profile ceiling by the total response weight in the two cones.

The limiting source equations and menu formula check:

    2x+3z=1,  256 x z^2(x−z)=alpha;
    r_i=1−4y_i, q_i=256 product(y)/y_i,
    theta_i=(r_i/q_i)/B.

The local scalar derivative is 256/75, so the displacement is O(alpha). The unique normalized positive dependence gives uniform convergence over ALL active response menus, including menus with several representatives in one cone. The two-cone weight tends to 2/5<256/625.

A correction to an initial root objection is essential: a captured part of a source facet is a three-dimensional simplex with FOUR vertices, including the original retained vertex. Its volume centroid has coordinate y_k for k different from the removed and retained indices, and y_i+y_j at the retained index. The incorrect denominator d−1 computes the boundary section centroid instead. The correct calculation gives exact facet affine neutrality:

    integral W_delta =1/B,
    integral W_delta lambda_k=1/(4B).

Accordingly every affine test has exactly the same ratio beta_delta=1/B, and beta_delta−Gamma_4=O(alpha²). There is no O(alpha) affine advantage.

The coercivity dependency has c_4=7/320 and Gamma_4 c_4=28/3125. The weighted-strip dependency has constant 40 and holds for arbitrary nonnegative convex functions, including concentrating sequences. Subtracting a supporting affine function at the facet centroid therefore gives the uniform nonaffine loss in (13). The coefficient bound sup|ell|<=3072 integral(phi) follows from the indicated corner simplex; it controls the positive-width affine error without an unjustified compactness assertion for normalized convex functions.

For the shared-patch observability estimate, E_i has scale delta/4, normalized three-volume delta³/64, and every facet barycentric coordinate at least delta/16. In the negative-coefficient alternative, the corner scale eta/[2(M+eta)] gives integral ell_- >=eta^4/[16(M+eta)^3]. Both branches imply (14) with the conservative constant 2^−23. Since f>=ell_- and phi>=ell_+, the stated delta^4 estimate (15) follows.

At each common facet normal, convexity at bases −1,0,1 forces endpoint boundary cost at least twice the source cost on the common patch. The remaining endpoint normals only add cost and all have profile below Gamma_4 by a uniform amount. Thus the entire normal-dependent nonnegative convex physical cone is covered, not just a finite selection of fields. Combining the delta^4 observability loss with alpha²=O(delta^6), and then choosing h small for fixed delta, gives a uniform STRICT efficiency deficit. All choices are sequential and have positive margins.

Scope: the example has one heavy middle fiber and its depth is well above the n=1 OC target. It rules out a universal individual-source Gamma_d lemma even after optimizing over all actual active menus. It does not rule out a global parity budget, a result conditional on a below-OC body minimum, or signed-field information from that minimum.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
